title: NASA Briefing to Highlight Contributions to Martian Moons Mission
text:
Media are invited to join NASA for a media teleconference at 4 p.m. EDT, Thursday, Oct. 15, to preview the agency’s contributions to JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission. The mission is scheduled to launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan on Monday, Oct. 19 EDT (Tuesday, Oct. 20 JST).

Audio of the media teleconference will stream on the agency’s website at:

https://www.nasa.gov/live

Participants in the briefing, who will provide an overview of the mission and NASA’s contributions, include:

Lindsay Hays, acting director, Planetary Science Division, NASA Headquarters in Washington

Tom Statler, MMX program executive and scientist, Planetary Science Division, NASA Headquarters

David Lawrence, MEGANE (Mars-moon Exploration with Gamma-rays and Neutrons) principal investigator, Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory

Kris Zacny, vice president, Blue Origin’s Honeybee Robotics

Media interested in participating by phone must RSVP no later than two hours prior to the start of the teleconference to Molly Wasser at molly.l.wasser@nasa.gov . A copy of NASA’s media accreditation policy is online.

The MMX spacecraft will arrive at Mars in August 2027 to begin its survey of the Red Planet’s two moons, Phobos and Deimos. After surveying Phobos in detail, the spacecraft will collect a sample of the moon’s surface no earlier than December 2028 and deliver it to Earth in 2031. NASA’s contributions to the mission include the MEGANE gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer, the spacecraft’s surface sampler mechanism, and communications and navigation support from the agency’s Deep Space Network , as well as funding United States scientists participating on the MMX science team.

The MEGANE instrument was developed by Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory. Honeybee Robotics, a Blue Origin company, developed the spacecraft’s pneumatic sampler mechanism. NASA’s contributions to the MMX mission were funded by the agency’s Discovery Program, which provides frequent flight opportunities for high-value, focused planetary science investigations. The Discovery Program is managed by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, for the agency’s Science Mission Directorate in Washington.

For more information about the MMX mission, visit:

https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mmx/

Karen Fox / Alana Johnson Headquarters, Washington 240-285-5155 / 202-672-4780 karen.c.fox@nasa.gov / alana.r.johnson@nasa.gov

zhTitle: NASA 簡報將重點介紹對火星衛星任務的貢獻
zh:
媒體受邀於美東時間10月15日（星期四）下午4點參加NASA的媒體電話會議，以預覽該機構對JAXA（日本宇宙航空研究開發機構）火星衛星探索任務（Martian Moons eXploration，MMX）的貢獻。該任務計劃於美東時間10月19日（星期一）從日本種子島太空中心發射（日本標準時間10月20日星期二）。

媒體電話會議的音訊將在NASA網站上直播：

https://www.nasa.gov/live

簡報的參與者將介紹該任務及NASA的貢獻，包括：

Lindsay Hays，美國華盛頓NASA總部行星科學部代理主任

Tom Statler，MMX任務執行官及科學家，NASA總部行星科學部

David Lawrence，MEGANE（火星衛星伽馬與中子探索）首席研究員，約翰霍普金斯應用物理實驗室

Kris Zacny，Blue Origin子公司Honeybee Robotics副總裁

有意通過電話參與的媒體必須在電話會議開始前不遲於兩小時向Molly Wasser（molly.l.wasser@nasa.gov）RSVP。NASA的媒體認證政策副本可在網上查詢。

MMX太空船將於2027年8月到達火星，開始對火星的兩個衛星—火衛一（Phobos）和火衛二（Deimos）進行勘測。在詳細勘測火衛一後，太空船將於不早於2028年12月收集該衛星表面樣本，並於2031年將樣本送回地球。NASA對該任務的貢獻包括MEGANE伽馬射線與中子光譜儀、太空船表面取樣機構，以及來自NASA深空網絡的通訊與導航支持，並資助參與MMX科學團隊的美國科學家。

MEGANE儀器由約翰霍普金斯應用物理實驗室開發。Honeybee Robotics（Blue Origin公司）開發了太空船的氣動取樣機構。NASA對MMX任務的貢獻由NASA發現計劃資助，該計劃為高價值、專注的行星科學調查提供頻繁的飛行機會。發現計劃由阿拉巴馬州亨茨維爾NASA馬歇爾太空飛行中心管理，服務於華盛頓NASA科學任務總署。

欲了解更多MMX任務信息，請訪問：

https://science.nasa.gov/mission/mmx/

聯絡人：Karen Fox / Alana Johnson 華盛頓總部 240-285-5155 / 202-672-4780 karen.c.fox@nasa.gov / alana.r.johnson@nasa.gov
